The former Hope United Reformed Church in Chapel Street, Salford , dates from 1819 Close to Manchester city centre and less than 100 yards from Salford Central railway station it ceased to be a regular place of worship several years ago. Grade II listed, it is now up for sale for offers in excess of £1.4m Its roots lie in a surge of "Christian fervour" across the country at the end of the Napoleonic Wars. It sprang from a dearth of places to hear the Gospel in the rapidly industrialising Salford. It survived as a church through name changes, and the resignation of its first leader A dwindling congregation eventually meant a final Sunday Service was held in 2019. In 2023 plans to convert it into a complex of flats, a community centre and commercial use were submitted to the City Council Hope United Reformed Church on Chapel St, Salford, pictured today. It is up for sale for £1.4m. (Image: Manchester Evening News)

Grade II listed, it is now up for sale for offers in excess of £1.4m Its roots lie in a surge of "Christian fervour" across the country at the end of the Napoleonic Wars. It survived as a church through name changes, and the resignation of its first leader A dwindling congregation eventually meant a final Sunday Service was held in 2019. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade.
